1. Transportation
(1) Streets
The street repair activity, described in Part III, will have a major positive effect on the area. Not only will the repairs serve to aid traffic flow, make the residential areas more accessible, and improve the physical appearance of the area, but it will have a positive psychological effect on project residents. The street repair work will demonstrate to project residents that the City is doing its part in improving the area (the same holds true for some of the other public improvements but to a lesser degree); and therefore, they will be encouraged to rehabilitate their properties in cooperation with the overall plan for the area.
Additional negative aspects of street construction have already been covered under "Atmosphere" and "Noise Levels" above.
(2) Public Transportation
Public Transportation will not be impacted to any recognizable degree by the project. The availability of ample public transportation, as is now available to the project, will be important to the redevelopment of residential areas along Front Street.
(3) Pedestrian
When completed, sidewalk and alley improvement will provide a major positive impact for pedestrian traffic. Some disruption of pedestrian traffic will be experienced during the execution period. The greatest disruptions will occur in the backyard areas where the old walkway surface will be removed and replaced. Other minor disruption will result from demolition and new construction in the area.
Pedestrians will also benefit from the increased security provided by the lighting in the backyard areas. Benefits will also be realized from the shade provided by the new trees and by the open space park areas. Restoration of the brick sidewalks in the area will help to maintain the character of the neighborhood, but the rough brick sidewalks will make foot traffic more difficult.
